paragraphs.exact_text: State x, predeclared constraint c, ordered codomain with units, zero boundary, tolerance ε, uncertainty interval [c_lo,c_hi], and optional grant-epoch budget B with cumulative consumption c_k.
Formal object

Given a constraint interval [c_lo,c_hi], define slack interval [s_lo,s_hi]=[-c_hi,-c_lo] and ε≥0. FEASIBLE iff s_lo>ε; VIOLATED iff s_hi<-ε; CONTACT iff -ε≤s_lo and s_hi≤ε; otherwise UNRESOLVED. For exact c(x), s(x)=-c(x). In the budget branch, s_k=B-c_k; nondecreasing c_k makes s_k nonincreasing within one grant epoch.
Constructor or predicate
Evaluate the fixed constraint and issue an interval-aware slack receipt.
Assumptions and cost
Constraint fixed before observation, units, order, evaluator, uncertainty, and tolerance.
Preservation account
A6 boundary, A13 route, original constraint, interval, units, tolerance, grant epoch, resource ledger, and sensitivity evidence. Work stutter may consume slack.
Predecessor and strictness
A cadence with no quantitative constraint is a predecessor countermodel; a gradient requires added differentiability.
Claim class and status
Scalar/interval minimum; vector and gradient extensions are branches.
Tests and falsifier

Known feasible/contact/violated fixtures including equality at ±ε; cross-regime interval -> UNRESOLVED; monotone-consumption budget fixture; stutter-with-resource-use; top-up-as-new-epoch; units, post-hoc constraint, tolerance mutation, and no-gradient default.
Authority ceiling
No ethical permission, value judgment, free scalarization, or mandatory gradient.
Residual
Vector aggregation, nonsmooth sensitivity, partial observation, norms, and gradient laws.
Return-to-PAL handle
Any constraint/unit/tolerance/interval/evaluator/route change reopens the assessment. A top-up opens a new receipted grant epoch; it does not reset spent budget.
